conversion_gaps.gap: No itemised furnishing quote given — only a £4,000-£6,000 range for an unfurnished 2-bed, despite the lead completing within 1-2 weeks and needing a concrete fit-out cost decision immediately.
conversion_gaps.evidence: Probably looking in the region as sort of four to six thousand pounds, I'd say, to do that.
conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Generate the itemised setup quote before next contact (ref reserved SQ-2026-079 per intelligence doc, not yet generated) so the fit-out decision can be made alongside completion.

conversion_gaps.gap: No second meeting booked — lead proposed 'another meeting' but no date/time was captured or sent via Calendly.
conversion_gaps.evidence: Not currently going. Probably the best thing for another meeting now.
conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Propose specific meeting slots within 48 hours, before the 1-2 week completion window closes and the furnishing decision has to be made without Stayful.

conversion_gaps.gap: Guaranteed-rent expectation never fully reconciled — lead's opening framing ('maximise rent and get guaranteed income') was answered with a flat no-guarantee disclaimer rather than a direct guaranteed-vs-maximise comparison, and the contradiction was never explicitly resolved in his favour.
conversion_gaps.evidence: I'd rather get guaranteed income and work with individual or team to manage that.
conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Directly address the 'guaranteed vs maximise' contradiction early with a side-by-side floor comparison (LTL guaranteed £640/mo vs STL worst-month £931/best-average £1,577) so the guarantee-seeking need is met with real numbers, not just a disclaimer.

conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Give the direct number verbally in the moment, or follow up by text within the hour rather than folding it into a later email.

positive_shift_moments.what_caused_shift: Framing the seasonal worst-case (January net ~£900-£1,000) as already matching or beating the guaranteed-rent figures he had seen elsewhere (£850-£1,000).
positive_shift_moments.lead_response: Make sense? You know, I'll thank you. What's your direct line to call you?

positive_shift_moments.what_caused_shift: Smart thermostat offered as a remote cost-control answer to his bills/utility-cost worry.
positive_shift_moments.lead_response: Moved on from the bills objection to asking about the peak-month upside rather than pressing further.

positive_shift_moments.what_caused_shift: Being given an open choice of rolling vs fixed-term contract rather than being pushed toward the longer commitment.
positive_shift_moments.lead_response: Engaged further with a detailed void-period question rather than disengaging.

friction_moments.what_caused_friction: Zac's first answer to the guaranteed-rent question was a flat 'we don't offer guaranteed returns' before any reassuring data was given.
friction_moments.lead_response: Continued pressing indirectly, later raising the three-month-void-period fear.
friction_moments.recovery_attempted: Zac followed up immediately with average/best/worst-case figures.

friction_moments.what_caused_friction: Lead's void-period fear ('three months and no bookings, left with nothing') was first met with a personal-experience reassurance ('I've never had that') rather than data.
friction_moments.lead_response: Pressed further, asking directly for 'the worst figure' rather than accepting the anecdotal reassurance.
friction_moments.recovery_attempted: Zac supplied the January worst-case net figure (~£900-£1,000).

friction_moments.what_caused_friction: Bills responsibility (electric, water, Wi-Fi, council tax all owner-paid) came as new information, and the lead worried a guest could run up utility costs with no control from 45 miles away.
friction_moments.lead_response: Pushed further on unpredictable costs (electric vehicle charging etc.).

zac_language.numbers_framing: Leads with the average/expected net figure first (~£19k/yr, £1,500-1,600/mo), then anchors the floor (January worst-case ~£900-£1,000) directly against the lead's own guaranteed-rent competitor figure (£850-£1,000), then closes with the ceiling (August ~£2,200-£2,300) — average, then floor, then ceiling.
zac_language.objection_handling_pattern: On the guaranteed-income objection: states plainly that Stayful doesn't guarantee returns and frames it as an industry norm, then immediately pivots to average/best/worst-case data rather than debating the principle. On the void-period objection: leads with personal track record ('I've never had that') before backing it with the actual worst-case number.

what_they_focused_on: contract commitment length and void-period risk
furnishing cost as an immediate cash decision
what_they_needed_most: a concrete worst-case number that beats the guaranteed-rent marketing he'd already seen
reassurance he wouldn't need to be operationally involved from 45 miles away
an itemised (not ranged) furnishing cost given completion is 1-2 weeks out
what_fell_flat: the direct 'we don't guarantee returns' answer, given before any supporting data, landed as a rejection of what he'd come in wanting
being told his direct phone number would come 'in an email after' rather than given there and then
profile_psychology_intersection.recommended_meeting_adjustment: For PURCH leads who open with a guaranteed-rent anchor, lead with the worst-case/floor figure before restating that Stayful doesn't guarantee returns — the floor number does the reassurance work the disclaimer alone can't, avoiding the early friction seen here. Also produce the itemised furnishing quote inside the call (or same-day) rather than a range, since this profile is often mid-completion with fit-out cash decisions due immediately.
